title: Maintaining Sanity: Algorithm-based Comprehensive Fault Tolerance for CNNs
problem: Hardware faults can corrupt CNN computations in safety-critical applications. Existing protection schemes either incur prohibitive overheads or provide insufficient fault coverage.
motivation: Safety-critical CNN deployments require consistent and dependable performance despite hardware malfunctions.
method: When hardware faults corrupt CNN calculations, this method detects and fixes errors at the algorithm level using hamming codes—math tools that spot and correct errors in individual data values. It focuses protection on critical computation paths and results rather than protecting everything equally, and uses checkpointing (periodically saving the computation state) to recover from severe faults. This targeted approach keeps runtime overhead to around 72% while correcting over 99.6% of critical faults—substantially better than traditional triple modular redundancy, which runs the entire computation three times.
key_novelty: Algorithm-based fault correction tailored to CNN-specific computations—using hamming codes (error-correcting math) and checkpointing (state-saving)—achieves over 99.6% critical fault correction at ~72% runtime overhead, substantially outperforming traditional triple modular redundancy.
contributions: Algorithm-based comprehensive fault tolerance technique for CNNs using hamming codes and checkpointing
Over 99.6% critical fault correction rate with approximately 72% runtime overhead
Minimal memory overhead compared to triple modular redundancy
Significantly lower overhead than traditional TMR while maintaining high fault coverage
primary_theme: algorithm-based fault tolerance for neural networks
